text:
release-lead: FYI rolling canary for v2.3.1 started 5m ago, seeing ~3x p95 latency on canary nodes. Auto-rollback didn't trigger. Noticed spike correlates with requests that include long context.
oncall-sre: getting alerts too. Oncall here — I'll pull up node metrics and routing.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: canary-latency-high - p95 latency 1.8s -> 5.6s on canary pool (3/5 hosts)
dinesh: I pushed a small change to KV prefetch in this build; possible cache thrash. Reverting would be safest if we can't stabilize quickly.
alyssa: can we drain traffic from canary while we investigate? We should avoid full rollback if we can do a quick fix + verify.
oncall-sre: starting manual drain of canary pool now. Command: ```kubectl label nodes canary=true traffic-drain=true && ./orchestrator drain --pool canary```
oncall-sre: drain started, traffic drop to canary at ~10% currently. Monitoring errors.
maria-cs: any customer impact observed? CS seeing a couple support tickets about slow responses in EU. Tagging known customers.
ben-qa: running smoke against v2.3.1 on staging to reproduce. If we can trigger locally, might be a config issue.
dinesh: I can run a bisect on the change set. If the KV prefetch is culprit I'll push a fix and we can reintroduce.
release-lead: if drain doesn't reduce customer impact in 15m, we should flip feature flag to disable the new prefetch path. Flag: `prefetch_v2` controlled in prod flags service.
alyssa: agree. Prep flip: ```flagsctl set prefetched_v2 false --env=prod --scope=canary``` - will coordinate with oncall.
oncall-sre: ready to flip, holding until we confirm drain status. Current p95 on canary is 3.8s (improved from 5.6s). Errors down 30%.
incident-bot: NOTICE: Pager escalation suppressed (manual mitigation in progress).
maria-cs: leaving a note for affected customers: "We're rolling back a change affecting request latency; mitigation in progress, monitoring closely."
denish: typo: starting hotfix build now with the prefetch guard toggled off. ETA 12m for canary deploy.
release-lead: plan B if hotfix doesn't land: full rollback to v2.2.x and traffic re-route. Please prepare rollback command set.
oncall-sre: acknowledged. Preparing runbook steps and will hand off to next oncall in 20m. Adding checkpoint: verify p95 < 1.5s and no customer 504s for 10m before marking resolved.
dinesh: pushed hotfix to canary, confirmed new image deployed. Re-running targeted load now.
ben-qa: initial synthetic shows p95 1.2s on canary after hotfix. Looks good but running extended tests.
alyssa: flipping flag anyway to be safe once QA green. Proceeding in 2m.
noncall-sre: flag flip done: `flagsctl set prefetched_v2 false --env=prod --scope=canary` :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: RESOLVED: canary-latency-high (mitigated) - monitoring for 30m.
release-lead: great work. Next steps: postmortem with timeline + why auto-rollback didn't trigger (metric threshold vs noisy signal). Assigning follow-up to dinesh and oncall-sre.
maria-cs: leaving customers notified: "Mitigation complete; we rolled back the prefetch feature in canary and are monitoring. We'll follow up with RCA."
noncall-sre: handing off to next oncall @dinesh in 20m for watch.
release-lead: thanks everyone. Closing thread after 30m successful monitoring.
